newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond and PIBOR futures ended lower but off their lows after a day dominated by technical factors and profit taking after several sessions of gains.
Dealers said investors were looking for reasons to sell and found several during the day.

Early in the session it was comments from French European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici who said that France would have to assess its public finances before deciding on whether to join the single European currency.

"There are other key dates ahead. We must assess the state of our public finances, and it will be in light of this situation that we will decide whether or not move to the euro," Moscovici said in an interview on Radio Luxembourg.
"The next six months will be absolutely decisive, and there will be political discussions between the Europeans to decide whether or not we begin the single currency," he said.
There were different views of the comments in the markets. One economist said though suspect, they could be seen as the first time a French official had so bluntly cast doubt on EMU.
"It was a live interview and we always know that live interviews are not totally reliable," he said. "But still, it sounds like a warning to the Germans."

But others said French investors were reacting normally after having pushed up markets in expectation of a successful Amsterdam summit. "It's a classic buy the rumour, sell the news reaction," one trader said. Late on Tuesday, a spokesman for Prime Minister Lionel Jospin disowned his comments.
Focus in the market later shifted to U.S. economic data, with stronger-than-expected May industrial production and capacity use providing the excuse to sell.
"Even though we got decent inflation numbers from the U.S., stronger industrial production gave us a good reason to sell," said one bond analyst in Paris.

He added that the market was at strong levels and that as the yield on the 10-year bond approached 5.50 percent, buyers were hard to find. On Tuesday, the 5.50 percent April 2007 OAT was yielding 5.60 percent after touching 5.54 percent on Monday.
Analysts said another softening factor was that investors were starting to accept that the single currency would be launched on time, but would be a more supple currency than originally planned.
"People are saying EMU will happen, but that it will be pretty flexible and therefore yield spreads will continue to converge but at a higher level than previously expected," a bond analyst said.
The franc weakened against the mark and the dollar, softening to 3.3741 per mark and 5.8475 per dollar by 1448 GMT.
